refactor(scanf): build the scanf engine and its arity wrappers as AST

The last of this branch's parsed-PHP preludes. The engine was 500 lines of PHP text tokenized on
every compile that touched `sscanf()` or `fscanf()`, and the sixteen by-reference wrappers were a
Rust loop that PRINTED PHP for the parser to read back — a round trip through text for something
already being generated programmatically.

The engine is TRANSCRIBED from the parse (`synthetic_class::transcribe_split`), so the twelve
declarations are the AST the parser produced rather than a careful retyping. The wrappers stay a
loop and build AST directly: sixteen transcribed copies of two shapes would have been sixteen
places for one shape to drift.

BOTH ORACLES ARE NOW PERMANENT TESTS, and that is a change to the gz conversion as much as this
one. `ELEPHC_ORACLE_WHICH` is a migration tool — it runs only when two environment variables are
set, so once a conversion lands nothing checks the builder again and the PHP reference becomes dead
code, which is what the compiler warned about after the gz commit. PDO had already solved this with
an ordinary test; `built_declarations_match_the_php_form` is its equivalent for each prelude,
comparing built declarations against the parse of the PHP they replaced, node by node, spans
stripped. 21 declarations for gz, 28 for scanf.

`strip_spans` moved out of the private `tests` module to module level so the oracles can share it.
Copying it into each would be three copies of a comparison rule that must not diverge — two
constructions of the same AST cannot agree on source positions, and every oracle needs exactly
that rule.

Verified: both oracles green, `cargo test -p elephc --lib` 1 530 passed, `codegen_tests io::` 1 024
passed, and the six scanf shapes measured against `php -n` 8.5.6 — array form, by-ref vars form,
both functions in one program, and a real file — all identical.

The compile path now parses no PHP for `gz*`, the zlib string functions, `sscanf` or `fscanf`.
What remains in the tree: `dir_prelude` and `mysqli_prelude`, neither this branch's.
EOF
